organization.name: Pacific Vision Foundation
organization.recipient: PVF general recipient; no confirmed restricted offer
partners: Lions Eye Foundation / CPMC Lions Eye Clinic
organization.region: SF clinical site and a conditionally SF-resident eligible cohort; the actual program also serves wider California and Nevada.

status: Constructed organization-specific conditional research estimate, not measured PVF effectiveness or a provider-priced offer

program.name: Proposed additional first-eye cataract surgical access through shared PVF/Lions pathway
program.unit: One eligible SF-resident patient assigned a supported first-eye surgical course; donor budget allocated across all assigned cases including failed referrals and noncompletion
program.coreCounterfactual: Expedited surgery versus otherwise approximately one-year delay, not permanent denial
program.clinicalScope: Visually significant first-eye cataract; clinical suitability, first/second-eye status, fellow-eye function and ocular comorbidity assessed by clinician
program.eligibility: Model uninsured patients meeting current Lions rules; do not assume insured/Medi-Cal patients admitted under this particular pathway.

funding.additionalityDefinition: Fraction of proposed complete surgical support actually expanded rather than replacing existing PVF/Lions/clinicalpartner financing; no effect on donation amount paid
funding.counterfactual: Existing Patient Assistance Fund, Lions funds, donated clinical capacity, ordinary referrals and any otherwise available coverage.

costs.interpretation: $1,000 gift-funded cash plus $2,500 of assumed partner clinical, facility and lens resources not already included in cash. This allocation is a research judgment, not a quote, charge or procedure valuation. No empirical leverage factor is used. Actual partner commitments and unused capacity are unverified.
costs.favorable: $500 complete cash support and $2,500 total direct resources; leaner additional support with substantial clinical underwriting assumed.
costs.pessimistic: $2,000 cash support and $6,000 total direct resources; more support and higher delivery costs.
costs.perspective: Conditional donor cash; separate gross complete-direct-resource diagnostic. Not a net payer ICER or full societal cost. The complete-resource diagnostic retains the whole modeled course cost despite displacement; participant time and future medical costs are excluded.

inputDefinitions.externalIntegratedQaly: First-eye one-year trial assignment QALY difference: .056 centrally and favorably; .006, the trial's lower confidence-limit coordinate, for the pessimistic stress. This is not a local confidence interval. Already integrated: no extra one-year, onset, success or falls factor.
inputDefinitions.clinicalComparatorTransfer: Judgment for local population, severity, comparator and pathway fit: .5 centrally and pessimistically, 1 favorably. Not a newly measured completion rate.
inputDefinitions.fundingAdditionality: Judgment: .5 centrally, .75 favorably and .25 pessimistically. A separate financing contrast; set to 1 if the clinical contrast already directly compares a gift with no gift.
inputDefinitions.sharedIncrementalHarmQaly: Extra local service harm outside the trial effect; scale only under identical replacement. Do not subtract trial complications again.
inputDefinitions.donorSpecificHarmQaly: Net extra privacy, disruption or other harm caused by donor activity independently of added surgery; outside the funding factor.

formulas.costCeiling: 10000 * netQalys; cost must be strictly below the ceiling to beat 100000 USD per 10 QALYs.

sources.title: 2025 Impact Report
sources.locator: Physical pages 7 and 16; patient stories elsewhere.
sources.facts: The Patient Assistance Fund covers surgery costs; 2,542 total surgeries and 570 total charity cases since 2020; shared regional CPMC/Lions pathway.

sources.title: Lions Eye Foundation services

sources.limits: No mixed-budget/procedure division or general leverage multiplier enters cost. No cataract-specific marginal quote.

sources.title: Falls and health status in elderly women following first eye cataract surgery: an economic evaluation conducted alongside a randomised controlled trial
sources.facts: 306 women over 70 with bilateral cataracts; 75% had baseline acuity 6/12 or better. Expedited approximately four weeks versus a 12-month wait. There were 288 economic-analysis participants. One-year integrated QALY difference .056, 95% CI .006–.108.
sources.limits: Assignment-level integrated EQ-5D-derived QALYs, not a utility level or an annual benefit forever. The mild-impairment older female sample is not all local cases. Indexed primary and independent-auditor verification; this auditor's full PMC fetch was challenged.

sources.title: Second-eye cataract surgery in elderly women: a cost-utility analysis conducted alongside a randomized controlled trial
sources.facts: 239 women over 70 with previous first-eye surgery and minimal remaining-eye dysfunction; four-week versus 12-month wait. One-year QALY gain .015, 95% CI −.039–.068, p=.59.
sources.limits: Important null counterweight, not a first-eye effect. Historical £646 net payer cost is not delivery cost.

sources.title: Cataract Surgery Cost Utility Revisited in 2012: A New Economic Paradigm
sources.facts: PORT visual outcomes and time-tradeoff valuations; 1.6212 first-eye QALYs over 13 years; 2.8152 bilateral QALYs; historical 2012 direct ophthalmic cost $2,653.
sources.limits: Different method and long-term untreated comparator, not a randomized lifetime observation. No societal economic ROI or bilateral total is credited to one eye. Historical cost is not a current SF quote.

rationale: The central estimate uses the randomized one-year delay benefit, halved for uncertain local/comparator fit and halved for funding replacement. The $1,000 cash amount is a bottom-up planning budget conditional on partner underwriting; neither that underwriting nor the marginal price is verified. This is a provisional best guess, not an evidence-weighted posterior or an available purchase. Favorable retains the trial mean rather than selecting the upper confidence limit; the low $250 cash case and long-denial model remain separate.
exclusions: One shared cataract pathway counted once under PVF; no additive Lions, PVF or CPMC procedure-health claims.
No first-eye benefit for every second eye; no bilateral QALY total for one operation.
No automatic health tail beyond one year in the core; fixture or lens duration is not the duration of counterfactual benefit.
No extra fall-prevention, independence, mortality, productivity, caregiver or monetary ROI gains.
No treatment of donated partner inputs as costless resources; no historical all-procedure budget/volume unit cost.
No assumption that all regional patients are SF residents.
No use of a Nevada patient's outside quote as a PVF price or an SF delay distribution.
acceptanceTests: Reproduce all core and separate scenarios with finite-input checks.
Q <= 0 returns null for both prices but retains signed Q.
Zero funding and zero donor-specific harm gives zero even with shared harm; donor-specific harm at zero funding remains negative.
No additional QALY multiplier for one year or trial completion.
First-eye, second-eye and lifetime cases remain distinct; only the central core is used for ranking.
No verified funding-room or priced-offer claims; recipient, partners and SF-resident restriction remain visible.

display.rangeType: Joint scenario judgments, not a confidence interval.
display.headline: Earlier sight-restoring care, with an uncertain donor margin.
display.recommendationBoundary: Real shared surgical pathway; hypothetical additional course and unknown funding room. Core favorable is above $100K per 10 QALYs; separate low-cash and long-denial sensitivities are not ranking inputs.
